A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SVBench study, with readable text, equations, four tables and four figures. All ten pages were inspected in each. Both end with references; neither supplied PDF contains the extended appendix mentioned in Section 3.1.

before.justification: v2 reports original evaluations of eight video generators in Table 2, prompt-pipeline and difficulty experiments in Tables 3–4, and human/evaluator comparisons and qualitative cases in Figures 3–4.

after.justification: v4 retains these original model evaluations, pipeline experiments, human comparisons and qualitative results.

M1.justification: The experiment-understanding, prompt-synthesis, critic and evaluation agents retain the same procedures. Cue manipulation, iterative prompt correction and five-dimensional binary scoring are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the thirty-paradigm suite and evaluate the same fifteen short-video tasks. The fifteen long-horizon tasks remain excluded from video evaluation; no new task or scenario coverage is reported.

E2.justification: Table 2 retains the same eight generators, including Wan2.2, which was already present in v2. Table 4 retains the same four closed-source models, and the pipeline-stage comparisons are unchanged.

E3.justification: Both use Gemini 2.5 Pro, five equally weighted binary dimensions, and the same difficulty conditions. Human alignment still samples twenty videos per model for a 160-clip test set. No reported evaluation setting changes.

E4.justification: The three-stage prompt ablation, cue-difficulty analysis, human/VLM alignment comparison and two qualitative cases are retained unchanged in Tables 3–4 and Figures 3–4.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals or significance tests. The reporting practice is unchanged.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 2–4 are identical, including Sora2pro's 79.6% and Veo-3.1's 72.4% overall scores. Figures 3–4 retain identical plotted results and qualitative cases; their relocation adds no findings.

T1.justification: Section 3.3 retains the same binary-score definitions and arithmetic-mean overall score. Neither version introduces formal propositions or proofs, and no mathematical reasoning changes.

C1.justification: The abstract replaces the assertion of systematic failures in intention recognition, belief reasoning, joint attention and prosocial inference with a less specific statement of limited socially grounded generation. The benchmark novelty, pipeline contributions and conclusion remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 3.1 removes the discussion of rare, long-tailed social interactions and its asserted connection to selecting robust evaluation dimensions. Interpretations of model differences, cue difficulty and human/VLM disagreement remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Implementation and evaluation disclosures are unchanged. The same project repository link is retained, moving from the author header into the abstract; no resource availability or access instructions change.

R1.justification: v4 removes three cited works and their associated passages: cryptocurrency reversal prediction, GRU-CNN-GA feature fusion, and curiosity-driven long-tailed learning. The positioning against video-generation and social-reasoning benchmarks remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The abstract is rewritten, three short passages are deleted, and affiliations, contact details and author-role footnotes are updated. The section sequence and most prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Table 2 moves from page 7 to page 6, Figure 3 from page 8 to page 7, and Figure 4 shifts columns on page 8. These are placement and text-reflow changes; figure content, table structures and captions are retained.

improvement.justification: Removing tangential cited passages makes the motivation more focused. The abstract's qualified summary also better accommodates the mixed performance in Table 2 than its previous assertion of systematic failures across named abilities. These are limited improvements in clarity and claim calibration; experimental evidence and reproducibility remain unchanged, and existing model-count inconsistencies persist.
